lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Part 1. You will hear a man who is carrying out a survey of people using a public library. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 6.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Excuse me. I'm doing a survey for the council about how people use Hilltop Library. Have you got a few minutes to answer some questions?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Er, well, I've got a bus to catch in about twenty minutes, so as long as it's quick.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: It won't take more than five or ten, I promise. Could I start with your name?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Yes, it's Helen Gaskell.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Is that G-A-S-K-E-L, with one L at the end?
lines.say: Is that G, A, S, K, E, L, with one L at the end?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: No, two. G-A-S-K-E-L-L.
lines.say: No, two. G, A, S, K, E, L, L.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Thank you. Your name won't appear anywhere in the report, by the way. It just helps me keep the forms in order.

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: That's fine.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: So how did you get to the library today?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: I usually walk, because I only live ten minutes away. But today I came on the tram, because I'm going straight on to my sister's afterwards.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Oh, so the bus you're catching is from here?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: No, sorry, I said bus, but I mean the tram stop by the station. Anyway, yes, I'm in a bit of a hurry.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Understood. And what brought you to the library this morning?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: A few things, actually. First, I had to print some forms for a job application. My own printer at home has stopped working, so I used the printer here. It's very cheap.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Good. Anything else?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: I'm trying to find a book about gardening. I've just taken over a small plot of land near my flat, and I've no idea what I'm doing! I've got plenty of cookery books at home, so I'm not looking for those.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Ha. That's a big project.

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: It is. And the last thing is I've come to collect a dictionary for my son. He's learning Spanish at school, and the library here didn't have one, so they ordered it from another branch for me.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: That's a useful service. Now, today's Saturday. Is that the day you normally come in?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Not really. I work on Saturdays most weeks, so it's unusual for me to be here now. I tend to come on a Friday, because I finish work early that day, and the library's nice and quiet in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 7 to 10.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Now I'd like to ask what you think of the library itself. What do you like most about it?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Oh, the staff, definitely. They're always so helpful. Nothing is ever too much trouble for them.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: That's good to hear. The study area was redesigned last year. What do you think of it?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Well, the new desks are lovely, and there are plenty of chairs. But there aren't nearly enough sockets. If you want to charge your laptop or your phone, you have to wait for someone else to finish.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: I'll make a note of that. Is there anything you'd like the library to have more of?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Let me think. There's a really good selection of magazines, so no complaints there. But they only take two newspapers, and they're both national ones. I'd like a wider choice of newspapers, including the local one.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: Right. Finally, I'd like to ask about the new library app that was launched in the spring. Have you used it?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Yes, I downloaded it a couple of months ago.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: And what do you think of it?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: It looks nice, and the search is quite quick. But what I like best is the reminders. It sends me a message two days before my books are due back, so I haven't paid a single late fee since I started using it.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: And is there anything about the app you don't think is needed?

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: Hmm. The map that shows you where each shelf is turned out to be more useful than I expected. But there's a weekly quiz on it, with questions about books and authors, and I really can't see the point of the quiz. I don't know anyone who does it.

lines.speaker: MAN
lines.text: That's really helpful. Thank you very much for your time, Ms Gaskell.

lines.speaker: HELEN
lines.text: You're welcome. Now I'd better run for that tram.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That is the end of Part 1.

groups.instructions: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
groups.title: Hilltop Library: user survey

is looking for a book about {4}

thinks the staff are very helpful

Opinions about the new library app

1.why: Helen spells her family name: G-A-S-K-E-L-L. Spelling must be exactly right.
1.trap: The man first writes it with one L. Helen corrects him: 'No, two.' Always wait for the final, corrected spelling.

evidence.quote: today I came on the tram

pairs: travelled to the library today by
2.why: The question is about today. Helen says that today she came on the tram.
2.trap: She usually walks, and later she says 'bus' by mistake, then corrects it to the tram. 'Usually' tells you walking is not today's answer.

3.why: Her printer at home has stopped working, so she used the printer at the library.
3.trap: 'My own printer at home' is not what she used today. But the answer word is the same: printer.

evidence.quote: I'm trying to find a book about gardening

pairs: is looking for a book about
I'm trying to find a book about
4.why: 'Trying to find' means 'looking for'. The book she wants is about gardening.
4.trap: She mentions cookery books, but she says she is not looking for those.

evidence.quote: I've come to collect a dictionary for my son

pairs: they ordered it from another branch
5.why: She has come to collect a dictionary that was ordered from another branch.
5.trap: 'Spanish' is the subject her son is learning, not the thing she is collecting.

evidence.quote: I tend to come on a Friday

pairs: I tend to come on a
6.why: 'Tend to' means 'usually'. She usually comes on a Friday because she finishes work early.
6.trap: Today is Saturday, but she says this is unusual for her. Saturday is the distractor.

7.why: She is happy with the desks and chairs, but there are not enough sockets to charge a laptop or phone.
7.trap: Desks and chairs are mentioned first, but she likes them. Only the sockets are a problem.

evidence.quote: I'd like a wider choice of newspapers

pairs: would like a wider choice of
I'd like a wider choice of
8.why: The library only takes two newspapers, so she would like more choice of newspapers.
8.trap: Magazines are mentioned, but she says the selection is very good. Write the plural form you hear.

evidence.quote: what I like best is the reminders

pairs: what I like best is the
9.why: She says the thing she likes best about the app is the reminders it sends before books are due.
9.trap: The look of the app and the quick search are things she likes, but not the best thing.

evidence.quote: I really can't see the point of the quiz

10.why: 'I can't see the point of' something means you think it is not needed. She says this about the weekly quiz.
10.trap: The map is mentioned first, but she says it is more useful than she expected.
